evidence.note: Full new-file diff present and untruncated (585 lines, single chunk part 1/1); no eval or other unsafe execution, no TODO/FIXME markers introduced.

Write uses staging dir plus rename-aside/rename-in/remove-aside; every failure path after MkdirTemp routes through fail() which RemoveAll's the temp dir, and a returned rollback restores the prior pack set.
shardPack validates every chunk against the measured diff (missing path, ByteStart>ByteEnd, ByteEnd>len(diff)) before slicing, so no silent empty-diff pack is emitted.
GC only deletes files matching the result naming pattern that are neither in the current plan map nor pass resultIsCurrent, so a counted result survives collection.
Validation evidence: package has a 1139-line test file; go test ./internal/shardpack/ -cover reports ok with 100.0% statement coverage.

findings.note: Prune is the only Writer method that does not resolve symlinks on root: Write, Discover and GC all call deps.EvalSymlinks(root) first, but Prune derives its directory from the raw root. If the caller passes a symlinked repo root, Prune computes a different path than Write wrote to, ReadDir returns NotExist, and Prune silently returns nil, so stale plan directories are never removed. Non-blocking (leak of stale pack dirs only), but the inconsistency is worth aligning.

evidence.note: Prune: dir := filepath.Dir(Dir(root, ...)) uses the unresolved root, unlike Write line 150 and GC line 369 which call EvalSymlinks.

findings.note: Discover treats any ReadDir failure on the results directory as 'no directory entries': the entries loop runs only under `if err == nil` and the error is otherwise dropped. A permission error or I/O error therefore looks identical to an empty/absent results dir, and the affected results are not reported in Found.Unreadable. Non-blocking, but a not-NotExist error would be better surfaced.
